description: Real frame cadences and tightened caps. Each case's derivation states how its admitted flashes were worked out by hand from the rules in this directory's README; tools/limiter-cadence-vectors.py checks them against an independent model of those rules and writes this file.

cases.name: cap-0.79-60hz-every-frame-onsets
cases.derivation: OSC-LIMITER-CAP-THRESHOLD. Every 60 Hz frame is a full-screen 1.0 onset; the cap is 0.79. Flashes are judged before the cap, so admission matches the default policy: 0 and 16.75 admitted; 33.25 refused (gaps 16.75/16.5 regular); 50 admitted (gaps 16.75/33.25 irregular) and the window is full. 1000 (0 has left, gaps 33.25/950), 1016.75 (16.75 has left, gaps 950/16.75) admitted; 1033.25 refused (window full); 1050 (50 has left, gaps 16.75/33.25) admitted. Admitted onsets are capped to 0.79, refused ones lowered to 0.4. Before the fix every frame came out at 0.79.

cases.name: slow-ramp-through-threshold-60hz
cases.derivation: Onsets ramp from 0.5 by 1/120 per 60 Hz frame, reaching 0.8 at frame 36 (600 ms) and 1.0 at frame 60. Frames below 0.8 pass unchanged. 600 and 616.75 admitted; 633.25 refused (regular); 650 admitted (gaps 16.75/33.25); later frames refused, the window staying full to the end at 1183.25 because 600 leaves only at 1600.

cases.name: slow-ramp-through-threshold-cap-0.6
cases.derivation: The same ramp with the cap tightened to 0.6. Detection is on the pre-cap onset, so the same three flashes are admitted and capped to 0.6, refused flashes are 0.4, and onsets from 0.6 to 0.8 are capped to 0.6. Before the fix nothing was refused.

cases.name: 60hz-jittered-every-frame-flash
cases.derivation: Every 60 Hz frame, its time jittered by up to 2 ms, is a full-screen flash; the default policy applies. 0 and 18.25 admitted; 32 refused (gaps 18.25/13.75 differ by 4.5, within 25% of 18.25 = 4.5625); 50.75 admitted (gaps 18.25/32.5) and the window is full. 1000 admitted (0 is exactly 1000 ms old and has left; gaps 32.5/949.25); 1018.25 admitted (18.25 has left; gaps 949.25/18.25); 1032 refused (window full); 1050.75 admitted (50.75 has left; gaps 18.25/32.5); the rest refused.

cases.name: 120hz-jittered-every-frame-flash
cases.derivation: Every 120 Hz frame, its time jittered by up to 1 ms, is a full-screen flash; the default policy applies. 0 and 9 admitted; 16.25 refused (gaps 9/7.25 differ by 1.75 <= 2.25); 26 admitted (gaps 9/17) and the window is full. 1000 admitted (0 has left; gaps 17/974); 1009 admitted (9 has left; gaps 974/9); 1016.25 refused (26 is 990.25 ms old, window full); 1026 admitted (26 has left; gaps 9/17); the rest refused.

cases.name: 144hz-jittered-every-frame-flash
cases.derivation: Every 144 Hz frame, its time jittered by up to 0.75 ms, is a full-screen flash; the default policy applies. 0 and 7.5 admitted; 13.25 refused (gaps 7.5/5.75 differ by 1.75 <= 1.875); 21 admitted (gaps 7.5/13.5) and the window is full; 999.5 refused (0 is 999.5 ms old). 1007.75 admitted (0 and 7.5 have left, one flash in the window); 1013.75 admitted (gaps 986.75/6); 1020.75 refused (21 is 999.75 ms old, window full); 1028.25 admitted (21 has left; gaps 6/14.5); the rest refused.

cases.name: 2.9hz-regular-flashes-60hz
cases.derivation: Full-screen flashes on the 60 Hz frame nearest each 2.9 Hz period (frames 0, 21, 41, 62, 83, 103, 124, 145, 166), dark frames between. Input: at most 3 flashes in any window, but 0/350/683.25 is a regular triplet, so it exceeds. 0, 350 admitted; 683.25 refused (gaps 350/333.25 regular); 1033.25 admitted (0 has left); 1383.25 admitted (350 has left); 1716.75 refused (regular); 2066.75 and 2416.75 admitted; 2766.75 refused. The strobe ban leaves 2 flashes per window.

cases.name: 3.1hz-regular-flashes-60hz
cases.derivation: Flashes on the 60 Hz frame nearest each 3.1 Hz period (frames 0, 19, 39, 58, 77, 97, 116, 135, 155). Input: 0/316.75/650/966.75 puts 4 flashes in one window. 0, 316.75 admitted; 650 refused (gaps 316.75/333.25 regular); 966.75 admitted (gaps 316.75/650 irregular, 3 in the window); 1283.25 admitted (0 has left; gaps 650/316.5); 1616.75 refused (gaps 316.5/333.5 regular); 1933.25 admitted (gaps 316.5/650); 2250 admitted (966.75 has left; gaps 650/316.75); 2583.25 refused. Output: exactly 3 flashes in several windows, never 4, no regular triplet.

cases.name: slow-ramp-sub-threshold-60hz
cases.derivation: Full-screen onsets ramp from 0 up to 0.79 at frame 33 (550 ms) and back down over 1.1 s at 60 Hz. No onset reaches 0.8 or the 0.8 cap, so there are no flashes and the output equals the input.

cases.name: mixed-red-and-general-60hz
cases.derivation: 60 Hz stream mixing general, red, combined and small-area frames; red budget 2. 0 (both): general and red admitted, onsets capped to 0.8. 100 (red): red admitted. 200 (both): general admitted, red refused to 0.4 (budget 2 spent). 250 (area 0.2): not a flash, onsets capped, red kept at 1. 300 (general): gaps 200/100 irregular, admitted; general window full. 500 (both): general refused (4th in window) and red refused. 1000 (red): 0 has left the red window, red admitted. 1016.75 (general): 0 has left, gaps 100/716.75, admitted. 1100 (both): general refused (200/300/1016.75 in window), red admitted (100 has left). Input: 5 general flashes from 200 to 1100 and 4 red flashes in one window.

cases.name: frame-rate-change-60-144-30-4hz
cases.derivation: Every frame is a full-screen flash while the host changes rate mid-stream: 60 Hz to 400 ms, 144 Hz to 800 ms, 30 Hz to 1500 ms, then 4 Hz (250 ms gaps, still credited). 0, 16.75 admitted; 33.25 refused (regular); 50 admitted; every 144 Hz and early 30 Hz frame refused (window full). 1000 admitted (0 has left; gaps 33.25/950); 1033.25 admitted (16.75 has left; gaps 950/33.25); 1066.75 refused (gaps 33.25/33.5 regular); 1100 admitted (gaps 33.25/66.75). 1500 and 1750 refused (window full); 2000 admitted (1000 has left; gaps 66.75/900); 2250 admitted (1033.25 and 1100 have left); 2500 refused (gaps 250/250 regular).
